en: The Questions of King Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes, Part One: The Lion Section.
10. The Question on the Python’s Limb “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one limb of the python should be adopted,’ which is that one limb that should be adopted?

“Great King, just as the python, though possessing a very massive body, remains hungry for many days and, being more wretched, does not obtain food sufficient to fill its belly, yet it sustains itself with only what is necessary to maintain its body even while it is incomplete;”
In the same way, Great King, for a practitioner of yoga, a bhikkhu devoted to the practice of alms-gathering,
who has approached others for alms, who looks forward to what is given by others, and who abstains from taking food himself— it is difficult to obtain food that fills the belly.
Nevertheless, a son of good family who is intent on the goal, having eaten four or five mouthfuls, should fill the remainder with water.
This, great king, is one quality that should be adopted from the python.
This was also said, great king, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:
“Whether eating fresh or dry food, ...”
One should not be excessively well-fed;
with a moderate stomach and measured food,
a mindful bhikkhu should wander.
Having eaten four or five mouthfuls,
one should drink water;
this is sufficient for dwelling in comfort.
“For the bhikkhu who is resolute.
Thus ends the tenth inquiry, on the limbs of the python.
This is the fifth chapter, the Lion Chapter.
Its summary verse:
Kesarī and Cakkavāka,
Peṇāhi and Gharakapotaka;
The owl and the hundred-winged bird,
the bat and the leech;
the snake and the python as well—
Therefore it is called a "chapter."
